events.title: Everything I Want to Do In a Show | A One Woman Show
events.summary: Hi, I'm Heather Sejnow. You may remember me from such things as that Christmas Commercial for a toy store that gets played every year near St. Claire Shores; hosting shows at the Senate or Redford Theatre as dead celebrities or film characters; or living in Chicago for a short while to do Second City, iO, and then hop back to Detroit to perform at Go Comedy and Planet Ant. I've even nabbed the title of the only female stand up impressionist in the state of Michigan ( that I know of) . I haven't been on a real theatrical performance stage in a while and I'm about to turn 40. So for my mid-life crisis I'm putting on a show of "Everything I Want to Do in a Show". It's campy, crazy, and heartfelt. Most importantly, it's a love letter to everyone I've met and all the vessels of creativity I've learned along the way. Oh! And it's interactive, NSFW, and there will be some prizes for attendees. So come join me on a wild ride filled with puppets, impressions, burlesque, song, dance, and even Shakespeare. It's definitely... "Everything".

events.title: THEATRE l She Kills Monsters
events.summary: Planet Ant Theatre presents SHE KILLS MONSTERS by Qui Nguyen, December 4-19, 2026, at Ant Hall. When Agnes Evans loses her teenage sister Tilly, she realizes she barely knew her. Tilly's Dungeons & Dragons notebook pulls Agnes into a fantastical world of epic quests, homicidal fairies, snarling ogres, and 90s pop culture as she tries to reconnect with her sister and find the courage she never knew she had. Equal parts comedy, heartfelt drama, and action-packed adventure, the play celebrates the power of great storytelling and the geek and warrior in all of us. Content advisory: Strong language, stage combat, sexual references, and themes of grief, bullying, and suicide. Recommended for ages 13+. She Kills Monsters is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Samuel French, Inc. For more information, visit www.concordtheatricals.com.

events.title: Performance of Jen Silverman's Witch
events.summary: In the town of Edmonton in Jacobean England, the devil has come to town. Scratch, a confident dealmaker, offers tantalizing gifts to townsfolk in exchange for their souls: Frank aspires for power, and trades his soul for it, while Cuddy, tortured with the fear that his father Sir Arthur prefers Frank to him, trades his own for Frank’s death. However, the soul Scratch wants the most in Edmonton is that of Elizabeth Sawyer, the town outcast, one dubbed to be a “witch” by a town that doesn’t know her... but to Scratch’s dismay, Elizabeth seems to be the only person not willing to hand her soul over to the devil. As Scratch continues to chase after Elizabeth’s soul, within Edmonton’s castle, tension mounts. Sir Arthur mourns his wife and contemplates on his inheritance, Winnifred grapples with the difficulties of being Frank’s lover, and Cuddy and Frank continue a silent war to win over Sir Arthur and his money. Cuddy and Frank’s conflict coalesces in a love confession and a murder, Winnifred seeks out the witch in town, and Elizabeth is finally convinced to give over her soul, in exchange the end of the world– this one, anyway.

events.title: Mazurka: Dance of a Polish Soul, Voice of the World
events.summary: The mazurka, one of Poland’s most distinctive musical dance forms, continues to inspire composers far beyond its traditional origins. While often associated with Frédéric Chopin, this recital explores the broader and evolving story of the mazurka through the voices of both celebrated and lesser-known composers from Poland and around the world. The program presents a diverse collection of works that reveal how composers have transformed this Polish dance into a vehicle for artistic expression, cultural identity, and contemporary creativity. It includes mazurkas by Karol Szymanowski, whose innovative language expanded the genre in the twentieth century, as well as works by composers inspired by Chopin’s legacy, including Zygmunt Stojowski, Julian and Nathalie Janotha. The program also features mazurkas by lesser-known Polish composers such as Wojciech Kilar and Mikołaj Piotr Górecki, whose individual musical voices offer new perspectives on the evolution of the genre. Special attention is given to the contributions of female composers, whose works enrich the mazurka’s continuing legacy. Alongside these historical works, the program features newly commissioned mazurkas created for the international 21st Mazurkas project—a visionary artistic initiative conceived, developed, and realized by pianist Anna Kijanowska. Bringing together composers from Poland, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand, the project presents the mazurka as a living international form. These contemporary works demonstrate the remarkable adaptability of the genre, blending elements of folk tradition, personal expression, modern compositional techniques, and diverse cultural influences. Each composer offers a unique perspective, transforming the mazurka into a global musical language while maintaining its connection to its Polish roots. Among the contributors is Matthew Bengtson, Associate Professor of Piano Literature at the University of Michigan, whose commissioned mazurka forms part of this international collection. All of these new works were written especially for pianist Anna Kijanowska and recorded on the award-winning DUX album 21st Mazurkas (DUX 2149). The recording received the Platinum Prize at the Golden European Piano Awards 2025, together with the Special Regional Representative Award (Cieszyn, Poland) and the Artist of the Month distinction. Through a dialogue between historical voices and contemporary creators, *Mazurka: Dance of a Polish Soul, Voice of the World* celebrates the mazurka as a living art form—one that continues to evolve across generations, cultures, and continents, while remaining deeply connected to Poland’s rich musical heritage. *This event is supported in part by the Weiser Center for Europe and Eurasia, and partially funded by a scholarship from the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage, Republic of Poland.*

events.title: Probing Chemistry Without Pushing It: An Electrochemical View
events.summary: For more than a century, electrochemical kinetics have been measured largely by driving reactions away from equilibrium, most famously through Tafel analysis. This works well when a single kinetic barrier dominates, but becomes much harder to interpret when several barriers contribute or when the reaction is so fast that moving away from equilibrium immediately brings in mass transport. We recently discovered that equilibrium current fluctuations offer a way around both problems. Because the system is not being driven, the fluctuations report directly on the underlying microscopic exchange processes, allowing intrinsic kinetic information to be extracted without the usual convolution with diffusion and with the possibility of resolving more than one characteristic timescale. We are now extending this idea to adsorption and desorption at catalytic surfaces which are the elementary steps often controlling electrocatalytic reactions but are difficult to measure independently. The fluctuation magnitude and autocorrelation function provide access to both surface occupancy and characteristic adsorption/desorption timescales. As we move into highly concentrated electrolytes, including the water-in-salt regime, we observe striking changes in these dynamics. The second part of the talk carries the same idea into a very different environment: using electrochemistry not simply to drive a process, but to uncover the thermodynamics and kinetics hidden within it. Here, the system is a biomolecular condensate formed by liquidliquid phase separation. The classic Miller–Urey experiments used electrical energy to drive chemical transformations relevant to the origins of life; in our case, we use electrical potential primarily as a probe of chemistry inside a highly concentrated biological phase. We recently found that entering a biomolecular condensate can fundamentally reshape the thermodynamic landscape of a redox reaction, an effect we probed by combining electrochemistry with OPTIR spectroscopy. One consequence is that a reaction that is nonspontaneous in ordinary aqueous solution may become spontaneous inside the condensate. We are now turning from thermodynamics to kinetics, asking whether the intrinsic rate constant itself also changes. This distinction is essential because reactions can appear much faster inside condensates simply because reactants partition strongly into the dense phase, without necessarily becoming intrinsically more reactive. More broadly, these studies ask how much of chemical reactivity is determined not only by the reacting molecules themselves, but by the microscopic environment in which the reaction occurs.

events.summary: Have U-M merch that is going unloved? Want uniquely personal, cool school spirit wear? Join us for the Patch-Up Pop-Up: Michigan Merch Remix, where you can transform your under-worn merch into something new! UM merch, patches, buttons, other embellishments, and blank garments will all be provided so that students, clubs, and other groups can collage together their very own maize and blue clothing. The Patch-Up Pop-Up workshop series aims to help students learn new, practical, and useful skills to revive and reimagine damaged or underutilized clothing items. Through a series of guided workshops led by an Arts Initiative teaching artist and supported by the Planet Blue Student Leaders and the VIPs Club, this series will sustainably divert clothing items from landfills, reduce consumption pressures, and stimulate circular clothing economies!

evidence.description: is a pianist and composer who treads fearlessly between genres, blending several styles and fusing Indian ragas with more traditional jazz into a style she has pioneered, called “raga jazz.”

featuredEvents.title: Everything I Want to Do In a Show | A One Woman Show
featuredEvents.summary: Heather Sejnow presents a campy, crazy, and heartfelt one-woman show featuring puppets, impressions, burlesque, song, dance, and Shakespeare. This interactive performance is a love letter to creativity and the people met along the way.

evidence.description: So for my mid-life crisis I'm putting on a show of "Everything I Want to Do in a Show". It's campy, crazy, and heartfelt. Most importantly, it's a love letter to everyone I've met and all the vessels of creativity I've learned along the way. Oh! And it's interactive, NSFW, and there will be some prizes for attendees. So come join me on a wild ride filled with puppets, impressions, burlesque, song, dance, and even Shakespeare. It's definitely... "Everything".

featuredEvents.title: THEATRE l She Kills Monsters
featuredEvents.summary: Planet Ant Theatre presents "She Kills Monsters," a play about Agnes Evans navigating her deceased sister's Dungeons & Dragons world. This action-packed adventure blends comedy and drama, celebrating storytelling and the inner warrior.
featuredEvents.registration: Online sales end 1 (one) hour before the start of a performance. If online sales are closed, there may still be tickets available for purchase at the box office.

evidence.description: Planet Ant Theatre presents SHE KILLS MONSTERS by Qui Nguyen, December 4-19, 2026, at Ant Hall. When Agnes Evans loses her teenage sister Tilly, she realizes she barely knew her. Tilly's Dungeons & Dragons notebook pulls Agnes into a fantastical world of epic quests, homicidal fairies, snarling ogres, and 90s pop culture as she tries to reconnect with her sister and find the courage she never knew she had. Equal parts comedy, heartfelt drama, and action-packed adventure, the play celebrates the power of great storytelling and the geek and warrior in all of us.
